To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Ge1-zC z/Si system exhibits a type II band alignment for all C fractions and that the critical thickness is a strong function of the C content.
the Ge 1-zC z layers are optically active for z < 12% and that the thickness for which PL can be detected gradually increases from 0.2 ML for z = 12% to 3 ML for z =6%.
the PL signal is observed only for C concentrations z 12% and that the PL intensity is strongly reduced for C concentrations z > 29%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for the production of Ge1-zCaz alloys.
the growth of Ge 1-x Cx layers with a thickness of 0.05 ML to 3 ML on Si(001), the determination of the band alignment and the optical properties.
the epitaxial and electronic structure of Ge 1-xC x/Si (001) heterostructures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for the Ge1-xCz alloy on Si(001), the epitaxial limit for optically active layers is 0.3 ML for z = 6%, 0.2 ML for z =12%, and 0.05 ML for z =29%.
for a C fraction of z 12% the epitaxial growth limits of Ge1-zC Cz on Si(001)-substrates are 0.5 ML for the monolayer and 1.5 ML for a submonolayer.
the PL of Ge1-zC Cz is observed for thicknesses of at least one monolayer and a C fraction of z 12%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ge1-zC z/Si system can be used as a model system for a type I heterojunction for z 29%, and as a model system of a type II heterojunction for 29% 12%.
for z 6% the PL signal can only be detected in the submonolayer regime.
the PL intensity decreases with decreasing C content and with increasing thickness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PL signal can only be observed if the Ge layer thickness is above the Ge-C intermixing limit.
the PL signal can still be detected for C fractions of z = 12% and 29% for layer thicknesses of 0.5 ML and 1 ML, respectively, and that these layers are optically active.
